label: Придя
description: A 10-sentence card for придя, the irregular perfective gerund of прийти.

missions.phrase: Придя домой, он сразу лёг спать.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: irregular -дя form, front position. Придя is the perfective gerund of прийти. It is irregular: instead of the usual -в, it takes a -дя ending on the perfective stem. It marks a prior completed action — he arrived home, then went to bed.

missions.phrase: Придя на работу, она включила компьютер.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: completed then next step. Придя reports the prior finished arrival; the rest followed. Note the irregular -дя suffix (not -в). One subject does both: she arrived, she switched on the computer.

missions.phrase: Придя в гости, мы подарим цветы.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: future main clause. The main verb is future (подарим), yet придя still fixes the earlier completed arrival. A perfective gerund orders events regardless of tense: arrive first, then give flowers, one shared subject.

missions.phrase: Придя на вокзал, я купил билет.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: same-subject rule. The gerund and the main verb share one subject: I arrived at the station, I bought a ticket. Придя is indeclinable, and its irregular -дя form stays fixed for any subject.

missions.phrase: Придя в класс, ученики сели за парты.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: plural subject, no agreement. The subject is plural (ученики), but придя takes no plural ending — gerunds never agree, unlike participles. The irregular -дя form is the same for all. Sequence: arrived, then sat down.

missions.phrase: Она устала, придя с долгой прогулки.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: gerund in end position. The gerund clause follows the main verb here, but the order holds: she arrived from the walk first, then felt tired. Придя keeps its one fixed -дя form wherever it stands.

missions.phrase: Придя домой, я отдыхаю на диване.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: present main clause. The main verb is present (отдыхаю), yet придя reports a finished prior action: I have arrived home, and now I rest. The irregular perfective gerund still means completion.

missions.phrase: Придя в магазин, он не нашёл хлеба.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: tight sequence. Придя (прийти) marks the arrival at the store just before the discovery. Built irregularly with -дя rather than -в, it still forms a clear before-then-after chain under one subject.

missions.phrase: Придя на встречу, мы долго ждали.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: prior arrival then wait. The arrival came before the waiting, and придя makes that order explicit. Past main verb with this irregular -дя perfective gerund, one subject throughout.

missions.phrase: Придя с мороза, дети пили горячий чай.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: everyday sequence. Придя names the completed prior act: the children came in from the cold, then drank hot tea. The irregular -дя gerund keeps the actions in order, all done by them.
